faq.a: Nectar is a sugary reward that brings insects and birds back again and again. While they drink, pollen sticks to their bodies and rubs off on the next flower.

faq.q: Why do some flowers smell bad?
faq.a: Flowers pollinated by flies and beetles, like the titan arum, smell of rotting meat or dung, because that is what those insects look for. The smell tricks them into visiting.
asks: Which flower smells like rotting meat?

faq.q: How far can insects smell flowers?
faq.a: Insects smell with their antennae, and many can follow a scent trail upwind from much further away than they can see the flower. Moths are especially good at it.

faq.q: Do flowers stop smelling after pollination?
faq.a: Some do. Snapdragons and petunias make less scent once they have been pollinated, so insects spend their visits on flowers that still need them.
asks: Why do old flowers lose their smell?

faq.q: Why do some flowers have no smell?
faq.a: Flowers pollinated by the wind, like grasses, do not need to attract animals, so they have no scent, nectar or bright petals. Many bird-pollinated flowers have little smell too, since most birds find flowers by sight.
asks: Why do grass flowers not smell?

facts: The titan arum smells of rotting meat to attract carrion beetles and flies, and has one of the largest flower structures in the world.
Many night-blooming flowers are white and strongly scented, which helps moths find them in the dark.
Petunias and snapdragons release less scent after they have been pollinated.

quiz.say: A white flower smells strongest at night. Which visitor is it probably attracting?
quiz.show: A white flower smells strongest at night. Which visitor is it probably attracting?
quiz.why: Moths fly at night and find flowers by smell, so night scent and pale petals suit them.

wrong.1: Most bees fly in the daytime.
wrong.2: Wind-pollinated flowers do not need any scent.
